html:
An ancient people of the central Balkans, in what is now Kosovo, southern Serbia and northern North Macedonia. The map shows their kingdom in 200 BCE.

The Dardani lived between the Illyrians to the west and the peoples of Thrace to the east, and ancient writers counted them sometimes with one and sometimes with the other. The geographer Strabo described them as wild people who lived in caves dug under dung heaps, yet loved music. They were fierce raiders of their southern neighbour, Macedon. Their kings, such as Longarus and Bato, fought Macedon again and again, and in 200 BCE Bato joined Rome against Philip V.

Rome conquered them in the 1st century BCE, and their land became part of the province of Moesia. Under Diocletian a separate province of Dardania was created. The emperor Justinian I was born there, near Scupi, the modern Skopje.
sum: An ancient people of the central Balkans, in what is now Kosovo, southern Serbia and northern North Macedonia. The map shows their kingdom in 200 BCE.
